title: Signal Gateway for Inference Metrics: OTLP Sampler, Prometheus Exporter, and Tenant-aware Enrichment
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Scope: Build a scalable Signal Gateway that consolidates inference-specific telemetry emitted as OTLP/Protobuf from inference sidecars and edge nodes, applies deterministic sampling and label enrichment, and outputs both Prometheus-friendly metrics (histograms/counters/gauges + exemplars) and OTLP-sidecar-compatible forwarded traces. Goals: reduce cardinality explosion from token-level labels while preserving per-request SLO signal, enable tenant-aware routing to downstream metric stores, and provide resilient buffering/backpressure for bursty RLHF/streaming workloads. Requirements: 1) OTLP receiver with a pluggable deterministic sampler (sample by request_id trace-root hash + configurable stride and seed), 2) label normalization and prefix-aware pruning rules (drop or bucket long prompt texts, normalize model and variant names), 3) Prometheus exporter that supports histogram bucketing tuned for token/response latency and exposes exemplars for trace linking, 4) remote_write and Prometheus exposition mode for Console retention tiers, 5) tenant routing with optional per-tenant aggregation windows and rate-limited forwarding, 6) schema validation and versioned contract (schema-v2) to support new KPI fields without disrupting downstream consumers.
notes: 2026-02-28: Triage meeting — identified cardinality and burst buffering as primary risks; proposed deterministic sampling to retain SLO signals.
2026-03-02: Design doc drafted in Confluence: /confluence/redwood/obs/signal-gateway-design (see related_links).
2026-03-04: Design review — infra + runtime + console attended; decision: keep sampling deterministic at request_id-level rather than token-level to preserve worst-case tail signals.
2026-03-06: Spike completed — prototyped OTLP receiver using otelcol with custom processor; benchmark: prototype sustained 12k rps with 128B proto events before backpressure on 8vCPU instance.
2026-03-09: PR opened for sampler and label normalizer: https://github.com/redwood-inference/obs-signal-gateway/pull/112 (see related_links).

2026-03-11: Review feedback from Security: add KMS-backed signing for tenant headers, and an allowlist for downstream endpoints. Marked security_review_required=false but will follow up with SRE for hardening.
2026-03-13: Performance bench run on m5-large-equivalent — histogram buckets tuned; p99 token latency aggregation shows 3.8x reduction in metric write volume with the deterministic stride=10 default.
2026-03-14: Integration test plan updated to include canary rollout to 10% of Dedicated infra and validation queries for Console dashboards.
Next steps: complete robustness tests (disk buffer, TLS rotation), finalize canary playbook, implement per-tenant rate limiter, wire up Console panels, schedule rollout with Platform SRE.
acceptance_criteria: OTLP receiver accepts inference events and applies deterministic sampling configured by request_id and stride.
Prometheus exposition endpoint emits histograms/counters with exemplars that link back to traces when sampled.
Label normalization reduces unique label cardinality by >= 70% for long prompt text fields in benchmark workload.
Gateway supports remote_write to our Cortex cluster and direct scrape mode for Console retention tiers.
Canary deployment runbook exists and a 10% Dedicated canary completes without SLO regressions for 24h.
Documentation updated: schema-v2 contract, config knobs, and troubleshooting section published in Confluence.
